title: Similes: ようだ, のように, のような and みたい
summary: ようだ is the far end of the scale: it makes metaphors and similes, with まるで for emphasis; みたい is its casual partner.

blocks.text: Think of a sliding scale. **そうだ** says how something looks. **らしい** compares it to a quality. **ようだ** goes furthest: it says "it is like this", and can build a full metaphor. All three can also end a whole sentence to mean "it seems".
**よう** is a noun meaning "form, likeness", and ようだ behaves like any adjectival noun: **ようだ** at the end, **ように** as an adverb, **ような** before a noun. A noun before it takes **の**.

blocks.jp: 彼女は風のように走った。
それは夢のような話だ。
blocks.en: That is a story like a dream.

blocks.text: ようだ after a whole sentence
After a whole plain sentence, ようだ means "it seems that": you judge from what you can see or hear.
Why ようだ is the furthest

Think of a wrestler. We know he is not really a mountain, so we only borrow one quality of a mountain: it is big and heavy. That is a simile: ようだ borrows one quality, and it never claims the two are the same.

blocks.jp: あの力士は山のようだ。
blocks.en: That wrestler is like a mountain.

blocks.text: まるで: here comes a simile
**まるで** (from 丸, "round, whole") announces an exaggerated comparison: "completely as if". It goes with ようだ and みたい, not with そうだ or らしい.

blocks.jp: 彼女はまるで人形のようだ。
blocks.en: She is just like a doll.

blocks.text: A whole clause: かのようだ

To compare something with a whole situation, attach **か** to the clause first. The か turns the clause into an "if": she did not really see a ghost, it is only pretend. That whole pretend clause then acts like a noun, so it can take の and ような.
まるでゆうれいを見たかのような顔をした。 She made a face as if she had seen a ghost.

blocks.jp: まるでゆうれいを見たかのような顔をした。
blocks.en: She made a face as if she had seen a ghost.

blocks.text: **みたい** is casual and an adjectival noun: みたいに, みたいな, みたいだ. It follows a noun directly, without の, and in speech the だ is often dropped: 羊みたい. It cannot do the かのよう trick, and it is not for essays. Do not mix it up with 見たい ("want to see").

blocks.en: It is just like a dream.
She is just like a sheep.

items: **Noun + の + ようだ / ように / ような**; casual: **noun + みたい**.
**Clause + かのように / かのような** compares with a pretend situation.
ようだ is the strongest of そうだ, らしい, ようだ for similes.

questions.note: A noun before the formal simile word takes the particle の.
questions.en: Her voice is like a bird's.

questions.prompt: このクッキーは雪の＿＿白い。
questions.note: ように is the adverb form, describing 白い.
questions.en: This cookie is white like snow.

questions.note: ような comes before a noun.
questions.en: Today is a hot day like summer.

questions.prompt: あの人の歌は、まるでプロの＿＿。
questions.note: ようだ ends the sentence; a noun takes の.
questions.en: That person's singing is just like a pro's.

questions.prompt: 彼の部屋はまるでごみ箱＿＿だ。
questions.note: みたい follows a noun directly, without の.
questions.en: His room is just like a trash can.

questions.instruction: Which does まるで NOT go with?
questions.note: まるで goes with ようだ and みたい, not そうだ or らしい.

questions.prompt: まるで何も見なかった＿＿帰った。
questions.note: か + ように: a pretend clause as an adverb.
questions.en: He went home as if he had seen nothing.

options: He wants to see a fish
questions.note: Noun + のように: like it.

questions.instruction: What does 見たい mean here?
options: I want to see the sea
questions.note: 見たい is want to see; みたい is a simile.
questions.en: I want to see the sea.

questions.note: Noun + の + ようだ.
みたい follows a noun directly.

questions.instruction: Which word class does みたい behave like?
options: Adjectival noun (みたいだ / みたいに / みたいな)
questions.note: Like よう, it takes だ / に / な.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that announces a simile
questions.note: まるで marks a vivid comparison.
questions.en: She sang just like a bird.

questions.instruction: Tap the simile that describes the noun
questions.note: ような comes before a noun.
questions.en: He has a face like a child.

questions.note: Noun + みたい.
questions.en: That cloud looks like a fish.

questions.note: Noun + のように: adverb.

questions.prompt: I heard a story like a movie.
questions.note: ような comes before the noun 話.
questions.en: I heard a story like a movie.

questions.prompt: That person is like a teacher.
questions.note: Noun + の + ようだ.
questions.en: That person is like a teacher.

questions.prompt: This room is as cold as winter.
questions.note: みたいに is the casual adverb.
questions.en: This room is as cold as winter.

questions.prompt: A noun before よう takes の.
questions.note: 夢のようだ style: noun + の + よう.

questions.prompt: Before みたい, a noun needs the linking particle as well.
questions.note: It follows the noun directly.

questions.instruction: Which says "as if he were sleeping"?
questions.note: Clause + か + のようだ.

questions.prompt: 部屋の電気が消えたようだ。
options: The light is like a star
It seems the light went out
I want to turn off the light
The light must not be turned off
questions.note: Sentence + ようだ: it seems that.
questions.en: It seems the light in the room went out.
